"""Alder Learning's term-end reporting job, with plotsrv added at the boundary.

All data are synthetic. One row represents a course cohort, not a person.
Run with --once to generate reports without a server; otherwise publish and
keep a small simulated portal workload running for the live log demonstration.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
from datetime import date, timedelta
import signal
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import PercentFormatter
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import requests
import plotsrv as ps

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUTPUT = ROOT / "output"
TEAL, GOLD, INK = "#247b80", "#bc7926", "#173e48"


def load_term_data():
    """Replace this reproducible fixture with the usual warehouse extract."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
    courses = {"Data analysis": 0.02, "Business administration": 0.01,
               "Early years practice": 0.03, "Health and wellbeing": 0.00,
               "Digital design": -0.02, "English for work": -0.01}
    cohorts, weeks = [], []
    for campus in ["Riverside", "Meadow", "Oakfield", "Online"]:
        for course, effect in courses.items():
            for schedule in ["Daytime", "Evening"]:
                cohort = f"AL-{len(cohorts) + 1:03}"
                enrolled = int(rng.integers(22, 49))
                capacity = int(np.ceil(enrolled / rng.uniform(.76, .97)))
                base = .89 + effect - .04 * (schedule == "Evening")
                base -= .025 * (campus == "Online")
                base += rng.normal(0, .014)
                for week in range(1, 13):
                    # A mid-term dip, then partial recovery; evenings dip further.
                    dip = -.065 * np.exp(-((week - 7) / 1.5) ** 2)
                    rate = np.clip(base + dip + .013 * (week > 9) + rng.normal(0, .014), .68, .98)
                    scheduled = enrolled * 2
                    attended = int(round(scheduled * rate))
                    weeks.append(dict(cohort_id=cohort, campus=campus, course=course,
                                      schedule=schedule, week=week,
                                      week_start=(date(2026, 1, 12) + timedelta(weeks=week-1)).isoformat(),
                                      scheduled_sessions=scheduled, attended_sessions=attended,
                                      attendance_pct=round(100 * attended / scheduled, 1)))
                attendance = sum(w["attended_sessions"] for w in weeks[-12:]) / (enrolled * 24)
                completed = int(rng.binomial(enrolled, np.clip(.89 + .5*(attendance-.85), .75, .98)))
                passed = int(rng.binomial(completed, np.clip(.86 + effect + .6*(attendance-.85), .7, .98)))
                fee = {"Online": 460, "Riverside": 590, "Meadow": 540, "Oakfield": 560}[campus]
                income = enrolled * fee
                cost = int(7400 + enrolled * 105 + (950 if schedule == "Evening" else 0) + rng.integers(-450, 451))
                cohorts.append(dict(cohort_id=cohort, campus=campus, course=course, schedule=schedule,
                                    enrolled=enrolled, capacity=capacity, completed=completed, passed=passed,
                                    attendance_pct=round(attendance*100, 1),
                                    completion_pct=round(completed/enrolled*100, 1),
                                    achievement_pct=round(passed/enrolled*100, 1),
                                    income_gbp=income, delivery_cost_gbp=cost,
                                    contribution_gbp=income-cost))
    return pd.DataFrame(cohorts), pd.DataFrame(weeks)


def make_figure(cohorts, weekly):
    plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 10,
                         "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
                         "axes.labelcolor": INK, "text.color": INK})
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8), facecolor="#fbfcfa", layout="constrained")
    grid = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=[1, 1.12])
    trend, outcomes, economics = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, :]), fig.add_subplot(grid[1, 0]), fig.add_subplot(grid[1, 1])
    fig.suptitle("ALDER LEARNING  /  Spring term 2026\nParticipation, outcomes & delivery", fontsize=19, fontweight="bold", x=.04, ha="left")
    for schedule, color in [("Daytime", TEAL), ("Evening", GOLD)]:
        totals = weekly[weekly.schedule == schedule].groupby("week")[["attended_sessions", "scheduled_sessions"]].sum()
        trend.plot(totals.index, totals.attended_sessions / totals.scheduled_sessions * 100,
                   marker="o", markersize=4, lw=2.3, color=color, label=schedule)
    trend.axhline(90, color="#7a8587", ls="--", lw=1, label="Planning target · 90%")
    trend.axvspan(6, 8, color=GOLD, alpha=.09)
    trend.set(title="01  Attendance softened mid-term, then recovered", xlabel="Teaching week", ylabel="Sessions attended", ylim=(65, 100), xticks=range(1, 13))
    trend.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter())
    trend.legend(loc="lower left", ncols=3, frameon=False)
    totals = cohorts.groupby("course")[["passed", "completed", "enrolled"]].sum()
    totals = totals.loc[(totals.passed / totals.enrolled).sort_values().index]
    y = np.arange(len(totals))
    outcomes.barh(y+.17, 100*totals.completed/totals.enrolled, .3, label="Completed", color="#a5ccc9")
    outcomes.barh(y-.17, 100*totals.passed/totals.enrolled, .3, label="Achieved", color=TEAL)
    outcomes.set(yticks=y, yticklabels=totals.index, xlim=(0, 100), xlabel="Share of enrolled learners", title="02  Completion is not the final outcome")
    outcomes.xaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter())
    outcomes.set_ylim(-1.3, len(totals)-.4)
    outcomes.legend(loc="lower right", ncols=2, frameon=False)
    for schedule, color in [("Daytime", TEAL), ("Evening", GOLD)]:
        frame = cohorts[cohorts.schedule == schedule]
        economics.scatter(frame.enrolled, frame.contribution_gbp/1000, c=color, label=schedule,
                          s=48, alpha=.8, edgecolors="white", linewidth=.6)
    economics.axhline(0, color="#7a8587", lw=1, ls="--")
    economics.set(title="03  Smaller cohorts face tighter economics", xlabel="Enrolled learners per cohort", ylabel="Direct contribution (£000)")
    economics.legend(frameon=False)
    for ax in [trend, outcomes, economics]:
        ax.set_facecolor("#fbfcfa")
        ax.grid(axis="y" if ax != outcomes else "x", alpha=.15)
        ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    fig.supxlabel("Synthetic demonstration data • 48 cohorts • 12 teaching weeks • Contribution excludes central overheads", fontsize=9)
    return fig


def write_report(cohorts, weekly):
    enrolled, completed, passed = cohorts[["enrolled", "completed", "passed"]].sum()
    attendance = 100 * weekly.attended_sessions.sum() / weekly.scheduled_sessions.sum()
    by_schedule = weekly.groupby("schedule")[["attended_sessions", "scheduled_sessions"]].sum()
    rates = 100 * by_schedule.attended_sessions / by_schedule.scheduled_sessions
    losses = int((cohorts.contribution_gbp < 0).sum())
    report = f"""# Spring term review
**Alder Learning · Management information · 12 January–5 April 2026**

> Fictional provider and synthetic data. This is a reproducible demonstration, not sector benchmarking.

## At a glance
| Measure | Term result |
|---|---:|
| Enrolments across 48 cohorts | {enrolled:,} |
| Attendance (learner-session weighted) | {attendance:.1f}% |
| Completed / enrolled | {completed/enrolled:.1%} |
| Achieved / enrolled | {passed/enrolled:.1%} |
| Direct delivery contribution | £{cohorts.contribution_gbp.sum():,} |

## What needs attention
**Evening participation warrants a closer look.** Daytime attendance was {rates['Daytime']:.1f}%
compared with {rates['Evening']:.1f}% in evening provision: a {rates['Daytime']-rates['Evening']:.1f}
percentage-point gap. The weekly table exposes the mid-term dip and subsequent recovery.
Contact evening tutors before week six next term to understand timetable and support needs.

**Track achievement separately from completion.** {completed-passed:,} completers did not achieve
the course outcome. Review assessment support by course before changing delivery plans.
These aggregate results do not establish why a learner did not achieve.

**Review smaller cohorts before scheduling the next intake.** {losses} cohorts had negative direct
contribution. Compare schedule and campus alongside cohort size; merging groups could affect
accessibility. Contribution is income less direct delivery cost, not operating profit.

## Explore the evidence
- **Course cohorts:** scatter `enrolled` against `contribution_gbp`, grouped by `schedule`;
  compare `attendance_pct` with `achievement_pct` to inspect the association.
- **Weekly attendance:** filter a campus or course, then compare `attendance_pct` by `week`.
  For overall rates use summed attended / scheduled sessions, not an unweighted mean of percentages.
- **Portal access:** open Suggested views → Errors or Busiest endpoints. Responses are genuine
  Uvicorn logs from scripted local traffic; 401 and 503 cases are deliberately generated.

## Definitions and limitations
One cohort is one course × campus × schedule. Enrolments are course registrations, not unique
people. Completed includes achieved; achievement uses all enrolled learners as its denominator.
Each enrolment has two scheduled sessions each week. There are no individual records or real
provider data. Random seed 42 fixes the extract; attendance patterns and outcome relationships
are modelling assumptions, not evidence of causation. Portal traffic is a separate demonstration
and does not explain the term results. HTTP suggestions describe retained events, not service uptime.
"""
    (OUTPUT / "analysis.md").write_text(report)
    return report


def run_portal(destination):
    """Follow the log before starting the producer: stream_view starts at EOF."""
    log = OUTPUT / "portal.log"
    log.write_text("")
    handle = ps.stream_view(source=log, format="uvicorn", label="Portal access", section="Operations", destination=destination)
    port = int(os.environ.get("PORTAL_PORT", "8011"))
    process = None
    try:
        with log.open("a") as output:
            process = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "portal.py", str(port)], cwd=ROOT, stdout=output, stderr=output)
            wait_for_server(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health", process)
            rng = random.Random(7)
            paths = ["/api/courses"]*8 + ["/api/timetable"]*5 + ["/api/attendance"]*4 + ["/api/session/expired", "/api/reports/export", "/missing"]
            n = 0
            while process.poll() is None:
                path = rng.choice(paths)
                requests.request("POST" if path == "/api/attendance" else "GET", f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}{path}", timeout=3)
                n += 1
                # Seed a useful screenshot window promptly, then keep modest live traffic.
                time.sleep(.08 if n < 160 else 1.5)
                if log.stat().st_size > 2_000_000:
                    log.replace(OUTPUT / "portal.previous.log")
                    # Uvicorn holds the descriptor; restart to open the new bounded file.
                    break
    finally:
        if process is not None:
            process.terminate()
            try:
                process.wait(timeout=5)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                process.kill()
                process.wait()
        handle.stop()


def wait_for_server(url, process=None):
    for _ in range(100):
        if process is not None and process.poll() is not None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Server exited; inspect {OUTPUT / 'portal.log'}")
        try:
            if requests.get(url, timeout=.5).ok:
                return
        except requests.RequestException:
            pass
        time.sleep(.2)
    raise RuntimeError(f"Server did not become ready: {url}")


def main():
    def stop(signum, frame):
        # The launcher can send TERM after a terminal INT. Do not interrupt
        # the Python/plotsrv exit cleanup a second time.
        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal.SIG_IGN)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)
        raise KeyboardInterrupt
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)
    try:
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="Only write CSV, PNG and Markdown outputs")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        OUTPUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        cohorts, weekly = load_term_data()
        cohorts.to_csv(OUTPUT / "cohorts.csv", index=False)
        weekly.to_csv(OUTPUT / "weekly.csv", index=False)
        figure = make_figure(cohorts, weekly)
        figure.savefig(OUTPUT / "term-performance.png", dpi=160)
        report = write_report(cohorts, weekly)
        if args.once:
            plt.close(figure)
            return
        destination = f"http://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('PLOTSRV_PORT', '8000')}"
        wait_for_server(destination + "/status")
        # The business job above produces ordinary files; these calls add live views.
        ps.publish_view(figure, label="Term performance", section="Review", destination=destination)
        plt.close(figure)
        ps.publish_view(report, artifact_kind="markdown", label="Analysis report", section="Review", destination=destination)
        ps.publish_view(cohorts, label="Course cohorts", section="Explore", destination=destination)
        ps.publish_view(weekly, label="Weekly attendance", section="Explore", destination=destination)
        while True:
            run_portal(destination)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
